advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a `--class duplicate` close whose recorded replacement is an inbound `supersedes` link (dead source) is named in the 'dead target / re-link' remedy, exercising _recorded_replacement_target's inbound branch.
evidence: close_precheck.py:129-134: `for link in inbound.get("inbound_links") or []: if link.get("relation") != "supersedes": continue ... return source`
_Store defines the slot but no test fills it: `def __init__(self, states, inbound=None)` and `find_inbound_relationships`, `lambda *a, **k: {"inbound_links": store.inbound}`

Interface-suite duplicate-class shapes (bug_duplicates_canonical, closed_duplicate_target, no_relation, archived_duplicate_target) all set outbound `duplicates` links via `rebar.link(bug, other, "duplicates", ...)`; none create an inbound supersedes toward the bug being closed as a duplicate.

ABSENCE: no test constructs a `--class duplicate` close whose recorded replacement is an inbound supersedes link with a dead/unresolvable source, so the second half of `_recorded_replacement_target` and its 'dead target' remedy on that path are unverified.
advisory.finding: The inbound-`supersedes` branch of `_recorded_replacement_target` (close_precheck.py lines 123-135) is never exercised by any test. This branch names a superseding ticket as the recorded replacement and drives the 'dead target / re-link' remedy for a `--class duplicate` close whose only replacement relation is an inbound supersedes link. The `_Store` fixture exposes an `inbound` parameter and it is wired into the monkeypatched `find_inbound_relationships`, but no test ever populates it, and the interface suite's `duplicate`-class shapes all use outbound `duplicates` links. A regression in the supersedes filter, the `from_id` read, or the ordering of the two source paths would pass the entire suite.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a unit case populating `_Store(inbound=[{"relation":"supersedes","from_id":_CANONICAL}])` with the bug having no `duplicates` dep and `_CANONICAL` archived/unresolvable, asserting the message names `_CANONICAL` and uses the 'archived, deleted, or no longer resolvable' remedy (not the 'records no duplicates link' text).

src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:88-91 `_has_live_replacement_link` returns True on a live inbound supersedes, so a DEAD inbound supersedes falls through to the new guard, reaching this branch
dropped.finding: The dead-target failure message hardcodes "its 'duplicates' link names {named}" but `_recorded_replacement_target` also returns the source of a (dead) inbound `supersedes` link. A duplicate close of a bug that was superseded by an archived/deleted ticket (and has no `duplicates` dep) will be told its 'duplicates' link is dead, misdescribing the actual recorded relation and pointing the operator at the wrong remedy.
scenarios: A bug with an inbound `supersedes` link from a now-archived ticket and no outbound `duplicates` dep is closed `--class duplicate`.
dropped.suggested_fix: Have `_recorded_replacement_target` also return the relation kind (or restrict the duplicate-close remedy to the `duplicates` dep only), and phrase the message per the actual recorded relation.
